subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw accept this coordinated set of action-pin upgrades across secret-bearing, release, scanning, and agent workflows after exact-head verification?
rationale: The patch changes executable supply-chain code under a protected security label; accepting the combined trust-boundary and rollback surface requires explicit maintainer ownership.

options.title: Verify and merge together
options.body: Confirm every upstream SHA, complete the direct Codex contract check, rebase, and require the exact head’s privileged workflow gates before merging the grouped update.

options.title: Split privileged actions
options.body: Separate Codex, token-minting, Docker publishing, and CodeQL updates from lower-privilege setup, labeler, and stale-action bumps for narrower review and rollback.

options.title: Pause the update
options.body: Retain the existing pins until the branch can be refreshed and the privileged workflow changes can be verified independently.

recommendation.title: Verify and merge together
recommendation.body: Confirm every upstream SHA, complete the direct Codex contract check, rebase, and require the exact head’s privileged workflow gates before merging the grouped update.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is repeated ownership of CI architecture, workflow hardening, action modernization, and Docker release automation.
